mainTopic: The miracles and events of the day ישראל crossed the ירדן, the hornet, and the split of the tribes on the mountains and the אפוד stones
overview: The amud opens by naming the author of the earlier ברייתא: it follows רבי שמעון. Then it describes the miracles on the day ישראל crossed the ירדן. They traveled more than sixty מיל to הר גריזים and הר עיבל, and no enemy could stand against them. A פסוק in שירת הים hints at two entries into the land. The גמרא concludes that ישראל deserved miracles the second time too, but sin prevented them. Next comes the rest of that day: building the מזבח, writing the תורה on the stones in seventy languages, the offerings, the blessings and curses, and carrying the stones to גלגל. A ברייתא says the hornet did not cross the ירדן. ריש לקיש and רב פפא each answer the challenge from a פסוק. Finally the גמרא returns to the משנה. רב כהנא says the tribes were split on the mountains the same way as on the stones of the אפוד, and a ברייתא about those stones is brought to challenge him; it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The earlier teaching follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view the previous ברייתא follows and answers: רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this? It follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the earlier discussion by naming whose opinion the ברייתא follows: רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous ברייתא held that nations living outside ארץ ישראל could be accepted if they repented. That fits רבי שמעון, who reads the command "לא תחיה כל נשמה" as applying only to nations inside the land, because only they could teach ישראל their bad ways.

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom? According to whose opinion?
The תנא whose view the ברייתא follows

phrases.english: According to whom is this?
phrases.notes: He means the ברייתא from just before this, on the previous part of the דף.

phrases.english: It follows Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion from before this section by naming the author of the ברייתא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא about the nations outside ארץ ישראל follows רבי שמעון.

steps.title: The miracles on the day of crossing the ירדן
steps.stepSummary: A teaching lists the miracles of the crossing day: a very long journey in one day, and no one could stand against ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and see how many miracles happened that day. ישראל crossed the ירדן and reached הר גריזים and הר עיבל, more than sixty מיל away. No creature could stand up to them, and anyone who tried was struck at once with diarrhea, as the פסוק says: "I will send My terror before you and confound all the people you come to..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic, a teaching about the amazing miracles on the day ישראל entered the land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Traveling more than sixty מיל in one day, right after crossing the river, was itself a miracle. On top of that, every enemy was struck with fear and sickness. The פסוק about ה׳ sending His terror before ישראל is brought as the source.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and see. Opens a teaching that shows something remarkable
Miracles
A measure of distance, roughly a kilometer
Was struck with diarrhea
My terror

phrases.english: Come and see how many miracles
were done on that day:
phrases.notes: That's the day ישראל crossed the ירדן into the land, in the time of יהושע.

phrases.english: Israel crossed the Jordan,
and they came to Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal,
more than sixty mil away,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין כׇּל בְּרִיָּה יְכוֹלָה לַעֲמוֹד בִּפְנֵיהֶם,
phrases.english: and no creature was able to stand before them,
and anyone who stood before them was immediately struck with diarrhea,
as it is said: "I will send My terror before you,
and I will confound all the people
that you come against, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: בֹּא וּרְאֵה כַּמָּה נִסִּים נַעֲשׂוּ בְּאוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching about the entry into ארץ ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the day of crossing, ישראל miraculously traveled over sixty מיל, and no enemy could stand before them.

steps.title: A second verse hints at two entries into the land
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק from שירת הים is brought as more support, and its doubled phrase is read as two entries into the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the פסוק also says: "Terror and dread fall upon them... until Your people pass over, ה׳." That is the first entry. "Until the people You acquired pass over." That is the second entry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second פסוק to back up the idea that terror fell on the enemies. It also reads the doubled words "until... pass over" as two separate entries into the land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase "עד יעבר" appears twice in the same פסוק. The first is the entry with יהושע. The second is the return from בבל in the time of עזרא. This reading sets up the conclusion in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And it says. Brings an extra פסוק as more support
The first entry into the land, with יהושע
The second entry into the land, returning from בבל with עזרא
Until they pass over

phrases.english: And it says: "Terror and dread fall upon them...
phrases.notes: שמות 15:16. The dots skip the middle words of the פסוק.

phrases.english: until Your people pass over, ה׳"
— this is the first entry,
"until the people You acquired pass over"
— this is the second entry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second פסוק to support the first one, and draws out a hint of two entries.
steps.raayaObject: That terror fell on the enemies when ישראל entered the land, and that there were two entries.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 15:16, with its doubled phrase "עד יעבר".

steps.title: ישראל deserved miracles the second time too, but sin prevented it
steps.stepSummary: Since the פסוק links both entries, ישראל were worthy of miracles the second time as well, but sin caused that not to happen.
steps.simpleTranslation: So now you can say: ישראל deserved to have a miracle done for them in the second entry just like in the first entry, but sin caused it not to happen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion from the פסוק: both entries were meant to be miraculous, but the second one was not because of sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the same פסוק describes both entries side by side, they were meant to be alike. In fact, the return from בבל happened in a natural way, with the permission of foreign kings. The גמרא explains this difference: it was caused by ישראל's sins.

keyTerms.meaning: Say from now. So we can now conclude
Worthy, deserving
That the sin caused it

steps.whatToRemember: The two entries into ארץ ישראל, with יהושע and with עזרא, were meant to be equally miraculous. The second came about naturally only because sin got in the way.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not say the second entry did not count or was not a real entry. It says the second entry happened without open miracles because of sin.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that sin can take away miracles that a people truly deserved.

phrases.english: Say from now:
Israel were worthy
to have a miracle done for them in the second entry
just like in the first entry,
but the sin caused it not to happen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the lesson from the doubled phrase in the פסוק of the previous step.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ישראל deserved miracles in the second entry just as in the first, but sin prevented them.

steps.title: Building the מזבח and writing the תורה in seventy languages
steps.stepSummary: After the crossing, ישראל brought the stones, built the מזבח, plastered it, and wrote the whole תורה on the stones in seventy languages, based on the words ״בַּאֵר הֵיטֵב״.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then they brought the stones, built the מזבח, covered it with plaster, and wrote all the words of the תורה on the stones in seventy languages, because the פסוק says 'clearly explained.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues listing what happened on the day of the crossing. Next comes building the מזבח and writing the תורה on its stones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new detail is that the תורה was written in seventy languages. The source is the פסוק's phrase ״בַּאֵר הֵיטֵב״, 'explain it well.' Making the תורה clear means making it readable for every nation.

keyTerms.meaning: Altar
Plaster or lime coating
Seventy languages, meaning all the languages of the nations
Explain it clearly. The source for writing in seventy languages

phrases.english: And afterward they brought the stones,
and built the altar,
and plastered it with plaster,

phrases.aramaic: וְכָתְבוּ עֲלֵיהֶם אֶת כׇּל דִּבְרֵי הַתּוֹרָה
phrases.english: and wrote on them all the words of the Torah
in seventy languages,
as it is stated: 'clearly explained,'
phrases.notes: דברים 27:8. 'Clearly explained' is read as 'in every language,' so everyone could understand it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks the timeline of the crossing day back up after the side point about sin in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תורה was written on the stones of the מזבח in seventy languages, learned from ״בַּאֵר הֵיטֵב״.

steps.title: Offerings, blessings and curses, and taking the stones to גלגל
steps.stepSummary: ישראל brought עולות and שלמים, ate and celebrated, said the ברכות and קללות, gathered up the stones, and slept in גלגל, as the פסוק in יהושע says.
steps.simpleTranslation: They brought burnt-offerings and peace-offerings, ate, drank and rejoiced, said the blessings and the curses, packed up the stones, and came and slept in גלגל, as the פסוק says: 'Carry them over with you and put them down in the lodging place.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the list of that day's events. It ends with ישראל carrying the stones and sleeping in גלגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The day did not end at the מזבח. The stones were taken along and brought to the night's resting place. The פסוק from יהושע is the source for carrying them to where they slept.

keyTerms.meaning: Burnt-offerings and peace-offerings
They said the blessings and the curses
They gathered up or packed up
גלגל, the place where ישראל camped after crossing the ירדן
Lodging place, where one sleeps for the night

phrases.english: And they offered burnt-offerings and peace-offerings,
and they ate and drank and rejoiced,
and they blessed and cursed,
and they gathered up the stones,
and they came and slept in Gilgal,
as it is stated: 'And carry them over with you,
and lay them down in the lodging place.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of events right after the writing on the stones.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the offerings and the blessings and curses, the stones were carried along and brought to the night's lodging place in גלגל.

steps.title: The stones were set down only at that one night's lodging
steps.stepSummary: Someone might think the stones had to be set down at every lodging place. The words ״אֲשֶׁר תָּלִינוּ בוֹ הַלָּיְלָה״ limit it to that one night, and another פסוק shows the stones were placed in גלגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think they had to put the stones down at every single place they stayed. So the פסוק says 'where you will stay tonight.' And it is written: 'And these twelve stones that they took...' (which יהושע set up in גלגל).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks a possible mistake about the פסוק it just quoted. The stones were not put down at every camp, only at that night's camp, which was גלגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״בַּמָּלוֹן״ alone could sound like every lodging place. The end of the פסוק, ״הַלָּיְלָה״, 'tonight,' narrows it to one specific night. The second פסוק confirms that the place was גלגל.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought. Introduces a wrong guess
The verse teaches. Introduces the words that block the wrong guess
Tonight. Limits it to one specific night

phrases.english: One might think at each and every lodging place —
the verse teaches: 'where you shall lodge tonight,'
and it is written: 'And these twelve stones
which they took, etc.'
phrases.notes: יהושע 4:20. The 'etc.' hides the key words: יהושע set them up in גלגל.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל בְּכׇל מָלוֹן וּמָלוֹן תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the meaning of the פסוק quoted at the end of step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That the stones were placed only at that one night's lodging place, גלגל, not at every camp.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יהושע 4:3 (״אֲשֶׁר תָּלִינוּ בוֹ הַלָּיְלָה״) and יהושע 4:20 (the twelve stones set up in גלגל).
steps.whatToRemember: The stones from the crossing were set up once, in גלגל, the place where ישראל slept that first night.

steps.title: A teaching: the hornet did not cross the ירדן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the צרעה (hornet) did not cross the ירדן with ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: The hornet did not cross over with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a new fact about the crossing: the hornet stayed on the other side. This sets up the challenge that comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the hornet had helped ישראל fight their enemies. The ברייתא says that help did not come along across the ירדן. This is a surprising claim, and the גמרא is about to test it.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught. Introduces a ברייתא
Hornet
Crossed over

phrases.english: It was taught: The hornet did not cross over with them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the stones to a new detail about the crossing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The hornet did not cross the ירדן with ישראל.

steps.title: Challenge: the תורה promises God will send the hornet
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the hornet could have stayed behind when the תורה says ״וְשָׁלַחְתִּי אֶת הַצִּרְעָה לְפָנֶיךָ״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it didn't? But it is written: 'And I will send the hornet before you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא with a פסוק. God promised to send the hornet ahead of ישראל to drive out the nations of the land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The nations named in that פסוק lived in ארץ ישראל, across the ירדן. So it seems the hornet must have crossed to fight them there. That clashes with the ברייתא, and Steps 10 and 11 give two answers.

keyTerms.meaning: And it didn't? Opens a challenge
But isn't it written? Brings a פסוק as a challenge
And I will send

phrases.english: And it didn't? But isn't it written:
'And I will send the hornet before you.'
phrases.notes: שמות 23:28. That פסוק goes on to say the hornet will drive out the nations living in the land.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא? וְהָא כְּתִיב: וְשָׁלַחְתִּי אֶת הַצִּרְעָה לְפָנֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ברייתא of step 8 directly.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that the hornet did not cross the ירדן with ישראל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה promises the hornet would go before ישראל to drive out the nations of the land. Those nations lived across the ירדן, so the hornet must have crossed.

steps.title: The hornet attacked from the bank of the river
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that the hornet stayed on the bank of the ירדן and shot its venom across. It blinded and sterilized the enemy, as the פסוק in עמוס describes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש says: the hornet stood on the bank of the ירדן and threw venom at them. It blinded their eyes from above and castrated them from below. As the פסוק says: 'I destroyed the Amorite before them… his fruit from above and his roots from beneath.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 9. The hornet did not need to cross the river, because it could attack the enemy from where it stood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both statements can now be true. The hornet went 'before' ישראל by hitting the enemy, but it never crossed the ירדן itself. The פסוק in עמוס, 'fruit from above and roots from beneath,' is read as hurting the enemy both above and below.

keyTerms.meaning: The bank of the ירדן river
Literally 'bitterness'; here it means venom
Blinded
Castrated them
The Amorite, one of the nations of כנען

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says:
It stood on the bank of the Jordan,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the hornet from the ברייתא in Step 8.

phrases.english: and threw venom at them,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the people living in the land across the river.

phrases.english: and blinded their eyes from above,
and castrated them from below,
as it is stated: "Yet I destroyed the Amorite before them,
whose height was like the height of cedars,
and he was strong as the oaks;
yet I destroyed his fruit from above,
and his roots from beneath, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: עַל שְׂפַת יַרְדֵּן עָמְדָה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets how the hornet went 'before' ישראל: it attacked from a distance
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Going 'before you' seems to mean the hornet crossed the river
steps.terutzMaskana: The hornet attacked from the bank of the ירדן without crossing

steps.title: There were two different hornets
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives a different answer. There were two hornets: the one of משה stayed behind, and the one of יהושע crossed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: there were two hornets, one of משה and one of יהושע. The one of משה did not cross; the one of יהושע did cross.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the same question from Step 9. The ברייתא and the פסוק are talking about two different hornets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hornet of משה helped in the wars on the east side of the ירדן, and that is the one that did not cross. A second hornet, the one of יהושע, crossed with ישראל, which fits the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Hornets
Crossed

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
There were two hornets,
one of Moses and one of Joshua.
The one of Moses did not cross;
the one of Joshua did cross.

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers to the hornet question: ריש לקיש says it attacked from the river bank, and רב פפא says there were two hornets.
steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: שְׁתֵּי צְרָעוֹת הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate answer to the קשיא of Step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the cases: two different hornets
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There was only one hornet, so it either crossed or did not
steps.terutzMaskana: The hornet of משה stayed; the hornet of יהושע crossed

steps.title: What does 'and the half of it' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about six tribes on הר גריזים. It asks about the strange word ״וְהַחֶצְיוֹ״ in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: six tribes went up to the top of הר גריזים, etc. What is meant by ״וְהַחֶצְיוֹ״, 'and the half of it'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic from the משנה. It asks what the unusual word ״וְהַחֶצְיוֹ״ is telling us.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word has an extra ה, like saying 'THE half.' That sounds like a split that was already known. So the גמרא wants to know which set split of the tribes the פסוק has in mind.

keyTerms.meaning: Mount Gerizim, where six tribes stood for the blessings
'And the half of it,' from יהושע 8:33
Tribes

phrases.aramaic: שִׁשָּׁה שְׁבָטִים עָלוּ לְרֹאשׁ הַר גְּרִיזִים כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: Six tribes went up to the top of Mount Gerizim, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה, which goes on to quote the פסוק in יהושע 8:33.

phrases.english: What is "and the half of it"?
phrases.notes: The extra ה makes it sound like a half we already know about.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the hornet topic and returns to the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which known division of the tribes the word ״וְהַחֶצְיוֹ״ refers to

steps.title: The split matches the stones of the אפוד
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers that the tribes were split on the two mountains the same way they were split on the two stones of the אפוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: the same way they are divided here, so they are divided on the stones of the אפוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question in Step 12. The 'known half' is the split of tribe names on the אפוד stones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אפוד had two shoulder stones, each with six tribe names. רב כהנא says the same six tribes on each stone were the six tribes on each mountain. That is why the פסוק says 'THE half,' meaning a group already set.

keyTerms.meaning: The two shoulder stones on the כהן גדול's אפוד
Divided

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
The same way that they are divided here,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means on the two mountains, גריזים and עיבל.

phrases.english: so they are divided on the stones of the ephod.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁחֲלוּקִין כָּאן
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The split of the tribes on the mountains matches the split on the אפוד stones

steps.title: A ברייתא about the two shoulder stones
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רב כהנא. It describes the two shoulder stones of the כהן גדול, each with six tribe names, as the פסוק in שמות says.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: the כהן גדול had two precious stones on his shoulders, one on each side. The names of the twelve tribes were written on them, six on this stone and six on that stone. As it says: 'Six of their names on the one stone, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to challenge רב כהנא from a ברייתא. This step sets up the source; the actual problem will be spelled out as the ברייתא continues.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the ברייתא only confirms six names on each stone. The challenge comes from the rest of the פסוק, 'according to their birth,' which tells us the order of the names. That order may not match the split on the mountains.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They raised an objection,' usually from a ברייתא or משנה
Precious stones
His shoulders
The High Priest

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁתֵּי אֲבָנִים טוֹבוֹת הָיוּ לוֹ לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל
phrases.english: The High Priest had two precious stones
on his shoulders,
one on this side and one on that side,

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוֹת שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר שְׁבָטִים כָּתוּב עֲלֵיהֶם,
phrases.english: and the names of the twelve tribes were written on them,

phrases.aramaic: שִׁשָּׁה עַל אֶבֶן זוֹ וְשִׁשָּׁה עַל אֶבֶן זוֹ,

steps.title: Only the second stone followed birth order, and each stone had twenty-five letters
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. The second stone listed its six tribes in birth order, but the first stone did not, because יהודה came first. There were fifty letters in total, twenty-five on each stone. Then the ברייתא introduces a second opinion, from רבי חנינא בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The names on the second stone were written in the order the brothers were born. The names on the first stone were not, because יהודה was written first. There were fifty letters altogether: twenty-five on one stone and twenty-five on the other. רבי חנינא בן גמליאל says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the ברייתא from Step 14, which it is using to test רב כהנא. The last line opens a new opinion, from רבי חנינא בן גמליאל, and sets up what comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the word כְּתוֹלְדֹתָם in the פסוק as describing only the second stone. On the first stone, יהודה was moved to the front, so that stone does not follow birth order. It also adds a detail: the letters were split evenly, twenty-five per stone. Both points describe how the stones of the אפוד looked, and רב כהנא said the mountains matched that layout.
